decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's node-gyp configure build, pinned as a production dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl per manifest-excerpt.json, with missing Visual Studio/MSVC evidenced from install-error.log; rejects general pnpm/network blame.

Quotes the top-level `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'` from lease-excerpt.md and explains that --ignore-scripts only defers the failure from install time to module-load/boot time because the entry must still resolve and load on Windows.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 with CreateSemaphoreW/Wait/Release bindings from the POSIX flock(2) on session.lock, noting Windows holds no file lock and fs-ext is dead code there; the plan keeps real flock on Linux/macOS.

Proposes a concrete pnpm patch of fs-ext@2.1.1 following the patches/node-pty@*.patch precedent: install script skips node-gyp on win32, entry gains a warn-once pure-JS flock fallback so the static import loads, registered under patchedDependencies in pnpm-workspace.yaml, plus reinstall, module-load and service-boot verification.
Explicitly honors the owner's no-Visual-Studio constraint and states the plan changes nothing upstream — local pnpm patch only, manifest pin unchanged, no fork or PR.
Cites full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 with its title, edge versions, surface and required-if-hit level, and connects its recipe directly to this fs-ext install failure and the Windows patch plan.

caps.reason: The plan is built around avoiding Visual Studio; any VS mention is a description of the failure, not affirmative advice to install it.
The report explicitly rejects --ignore-scripts alone as turning an install failure into a boot failure; the final plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via a patch.
The plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patchedDependencies mechanism and explicitly disclaims any upstream change to fs-ext.
The flock stub only affects the never-taken Windows branch; Windows locking stays on the named semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock, so no real write ownership is weakened.
